title: Renewal & Expansion Check-in: Capacity + Regions
summary: Renewal conversation focused on CoralPay upgrading to a larger dedicated capacity pool, adding an EU region for data residency, and agreeing preliminary commercial terms for a 12-month extension with a pilot uplift. Action items: Redwood to send pricing worksheet and EU region latency benchmarks; CoralPay to share internal procurement timeline and list of compliance docs required.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Priya Narang (Redwood CSM); Daniel Brooks (CoralPay Head of ML), Aisha Khan (Platform Eng), Mark Rivera (Procurement)

Auto-generated Summary: renewal check-in to discuss capacity increases, EU region add, contract extension options.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick check — can folks hear me okay?
[00:07] Daniel (CoralPay): Yeah, loud and clear. Thanks Maya.
[00:10] Maya: Awesome. I'll kick us off. We wanted to run through your renewal, the capacity request you submitted, and the ask about adding an EU region. Ethan is here for the technical bits and Priya will follow on ops and billing.
[00:25] Aisha: Great. We've got a short agenda, hopefully — we're mainly triaging timeline because legal's leaning on procurement.
[00:30] Mark: Yeah procurement wants a clear go/no-go by end of month.
[00:33] Maya: Understood. Quick reminder of current state: CoralPay's on a 4-GPU dedicated pool in us-east with 95th percentile latency targets of 300ms for your chat flows. You're averaging about 72% utilization and have spiky nights. The renewal request was for moving to an 8-GPU pool plus an EU read-only pool, correct?
[00:50] Daniel: Right. Primary ask is capacity for peak—especially during Euro market hours—so we need lower cross-region latency and data residency for EU customers. Also want to lock pricing for 12 months.
[01:05] Ethan (Redwood SE): On the capacity side, doubling to 8 GPUs should reduce queuing and bring tail latency down considerably. We also had a couple notes from your benchmarks last month — the kv cache patterns were large which benefits from bigger dedicated cache memory and continuous batching.
[01:22] Aisha: quick question — when you say EU read-only pool, does that mean data will be stored there? We need to be precise for legal.
[01:29] Priya (CSM): Good callout — we typically offer an EU region with isolated VPC endpoints and can keep logs/audit data in-region if required. We can tier what stays in EU: request logs and payloads vs audit logs. We'll map the retention policy.
[01:44] Daniel: Can Redwood support KMS integration with our BYOK (bring your own key)?
[01:49] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys; for Dedicated we have KMS integration options and HSM-backed key management on enterprise plans. We'll confirm the exact flow and any added latency.
[02:05] Mark: From procurement perspective, we need a clear quote with 12-month commitment discounts, and whether there's a price break for multi-region. Also licensing terms around private data handling.
[02:15] Maya: We'll put that in the commercial worksheet. Priya, can you note the discount tiers?
[02:19] Priya: Yes, I'll add our standard renewal uplift table and a multi-region discount option. We typically offer 8-12% off list for a 12-month commit and better pricing for 24-month. For this discussion we'll draft a proposal at 10% given your volume.
[02:36] Aisha: What about autoscaling — if we go to 8 GPUs, can we still autoscale for bursts?
[02:42] Ethan: Yep, our Dedicated pools support burst capacity and configurable autoscaling policies. For CoralPay we recommended a baseline of 8 with 2 GPU burst for high traffic peaks. That keeps cost predictable but allows headroom.
[02:55] Daniel: Do those bursts come from shared capacity or reserved? We need isolation for payments traffic.
[03:00] Ethan: Bursts can be from reserved spare nodes within your tenancy or from shared overflow. For strict isolation we recommend reserving burst nodes in your dedicated pool; that is slightly pricier but keeps traffic in your hardware.
[03:14] Mark: Slightly pricier is fine if it avoids audit headaches.
[03:18] Maya: On the EU region, there's two options: full dedicated EU pool or a warm read-only pool that routes requests and stores minimal data in-region. Tradeoffs are cost vs strict residency.
[03:31] Aisha: For now we need residency for EU cards data and PII — so likely full dedicated. Do you have latency numbers for eu-west-1?
[03:39] Ethan: We can share our recent benchmarks. I'll attach a spreadsheet with p95 latency from eu-west-1 to your app stack; generally p95 is ~120-180ms depending on model and sequence length. We'll include variations for the quantized model you run.
[03:55] Daniel: That would help. Also we're exploring a mixed quantization strategy to reduce cost — curious what Redwood recommends.
[04:01] Ethan: We recommend int8 for most chat flows; certain evals may need higher precision. Redwood Optimize can produce model-specific quantization profiles; we can run a quick loss-of-quality check on your prompt set.
[04:13] Daniel: Nice. Is that an add-on or included?
[04:16] Priya: For renewals, a base set of Optimize recommendations are included; deeper profiling is an add-on but we can include a one-off evaluation for your pilot in the quote.
[04:26] Mark: Timeline — if we sign by Feb 28, what lead time for spin-up?
[04:30] Ethan: For Dedicated 8-GPU + EU region dedicated pool, lead time is typically 3-4 weeks including networking and IAM setup; if you want BYOK and private VPC peering it pushes to 4-6 weeks.
[04:42] Maya: So procurement's end-of-month ask is tight but doable if we start paperwork now.
[04:47] Mark: We'll push it internally.
[04:49] Aisha: Another security question: SOC 2 scope and any penetration testing support?
[04:54] Priya: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we provide attestation; for penetration tests we can coordinate with our security team and provide guidance. For Private deployments we can support customer-led tests under a controlled window.
[05:07] Daniel: Good. On the contract itself, can we get a clause about fallback to hosted API if dedicated suffers an outage? We need RTO/RPO SLAs.
[05:16] Maya: We have fallback policies — automated routing to compatible model variants in hosted for short disruptions. SLA specifics and credits we'll outline in the SOW.
[05:25] Ethan: technically the fallback works but there may be differences in quantization and slight latency changes; we'll document expected deltas.
[05:33] Daniel: Okay noted.
[05:35] Maya: Quick interjection — are there any concerns about data retention windows or logging that we should capture now?
[05:41] Aisha: We need audit logs for three years and ability to perform export on demand.
[05:46] Priya: We can include extended log retention as an add-on — capture and export is supported. We'll list costs in the worksheet.
[05:56] Mark: Regarding pricing: is there a committed usage track vs pay-as-you-go? We prefer committed for predictability.
[06:02] Maya: Committed is the standard for Dedicated; we'll propose committed capacity with burst allowances. The quote will include the per-GPU effective rate and the discount.
[06:10] Daniel: Any risk of vendor lock-in? We want safe exit clauses.
[06:14] Maya: We provide export tools for models and KV caches; exit assistance can be built into the SOW for a one-time migration support. We'll propose a clause.
[06:23] Aisha: For the EU pool, are we able to route just EU traffic there automatically?
[06:27] Ethan: Yes, smart routing policies can be configured by geo + customer tier; fallback to US if capacity constrained is optional. We'll show routing config examples.
[06:36] Daniel: Can we get an SLA for cross-region replication times for caches? We're worried about consistency.
[06:41] Ethan: Cross-region KV replication is eventual — usually sub-second for small cache entries but we can surface exact replication guarantees in the tech spec. For critical session state we recommend local session affinity.
[06:54] Maya: Great. I want to propose concrete next steps so procurement can move: Redwood to send a draft quote with 12-month committed pricing for 8 GPUs + dedicated EU pool, include burst reservation pricing, multi-region discount, BYOK/ KMS integration notes, SOC 2 attestation and pen-test process, and expected lead times.
[07:13] Mark: And CoralPay will share procurement timeline and internal approvers list.
[07:18] Daniel: We'll also share the prompt set and evaluation criteria so Redwood can run Optimize checks.
[07:23] Priya: Perfect — we'll run a quick quantization/qc pass on that set and include recommendations.
[07:28] Aisha: One more — do you support SSO/SAML for role-based access?
[07:32] Priya: Yes, SAML/SCIM and granular RBAC are supported. We'll include the integration checklist.
[07:40] Daniel: Any competitors in the mix right now? We have an RFP and Anthropic and a couple of infra vendors are in conversation.
[07:47] Maya: Understood — we'll make the commercial case on latency and reliability, and include our benchmark docs.
[07:52] Mark: For the formal contract term, can we get a draft redline to review?
[07:56] Maya: We'll send an initial SOW and standard agreement. Expect it in 48 hours.
[08:01] Ethan: I'll attach latency benchmark spreadsheet and a technical appendix for the EU deployment.
[08:07] Priya: And I'll attach the pricing worksheet and renewal uplift table.
[08:12] Daniel: Sounds good.
[08:14] Maya: Anything else before we wrap?
[08:18] Aisha: Just confirm training windows — we might want a short onboarding or runbook for DevOps.
[08:23] Priya: We can include a 2-hour onboarding workshop and runbook as part of the renewal pilot.
[08:29] Daniel: Perfect.
[08:31] Maya: Okay great. We'll recap.

Recap
[08:35] Maya: 1) Redwood to send draft quote + SOW in 48 hours (includes 8-GPU committed pool, dedicated EU pool, burst options, BYOK notes, SOC 2 docs, pen-test process).
[08:47] Maya: 2) Ethan to send benchmark spreadsheet and technical appendix.
[08:50] Priya: 3) Pricing worksheet and renewal discount table (we'll propose 10% for this 12-month term).
[08:56] Mark: 4) CoralPay to send procurement timeline and approver list by Feb 19.
[09:02] Daniel: 5) CoralPay to share prompt set and evaluation criteria for Optimize check by Feb 17.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: some speaker attribution may be generic; audio had short overlap at 00:30-00:40 causing minor word swaps.
